records.text: Lori Frantzve appeared on the Arizona legislative floor in support of an electromagnetic-pulse preparedness measure sponsored by David Farnsworth and promoted recommendations associated with GTEC Industries.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: On the on the congressional floor, because she is she has David Farnsworth sponsoring a bill, she's doing this panic stuff, there could be an EMP event, and we have to get prepared for an EMP event that could happen electromagnetic pulses and here is what me and my husband Larry Guinta recommend that you do.

verification.notes: Arizona Legislature committee minutes confirm Lori Frantzve, identified as CEO of GTEC Industries, appeared with sponsor Senator David Farnsworth to support SB1476 on EMP preparedness and participated in a presentation. The episode's description of the appearance as on the legislative floor is imprecise; the record is a House committee hearing.

verification.notes: The resurfaced Black Start clip directly records Erika Kirk stating that her group presented five grid-vulnerability categories—cyber, hackers, physical threat, solar EMP, and man-made EMP—to congressional officials and that officials heard the risk analysis but did not want to act. This verifies her firsthand on-record claim; no independent congressional response record was located, so confidence is medium.

records.text: The CIA director appears in the documentary featuring Erika Kirk, CIA approval would have been required, and Kirk was discussing her mother's EMP business rather than acting.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Okay, yes, but the head of the CIA is in it. Okay, you gotta get approval from the CIA to be in a CIA documentary. That doesn't just happen casually. Like he says, are you getting that phone call from your agent? And no, she's not acting.

verification.notes: Black Start includes Erika Kirk as herself discussing EMP/grid threats and also interviews former CIA director James Woolsey. But it was an independent Heartfelt Films documentary, Woolsey was a former—not serving—CIA director, and no evidence supports Owens's claim that CIA approval was required for his participation. The EMP/self-interview component is supported; the CIA-control/approval component is not.
